title: Envisioning Beyond the Few: Disentangled Semantics and Primitives for Few-Shot Atypical Layout-to-Image Generation
claim: Existing methods yield fragmented, distorted outputs from few examples; disentangling semantic anchors from local primitives restores coherent generation.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; image grid with red error boxes, then diagram
description: The figure has two panels split by a dashed vertical line. Panel (a), Motivation, is a 2-row image grid. The first column shows 5-shot training samples with a blank layout box labeled 'chimney' or 'turtle'. Next to it are outputs from MIGC, CC-Diff and CC-Diff++, then 'Ours'. Red boxes and red italic labels mark the baseline failures: 'Fused Clusters', 'Duplicate Outlets', 'Malformed Base', 'Amorphous Shell', 'Multiple heads' and 'Headless Body'. The 'Ours' column looks coherent. Panel (b), Core design principle, is a schematic. A grey rounded box labeled 'Diffusion' holds dark blocks that look like a U-Net. Navy arrows from 'Semantic Anchors' feed the middle blocks, and green arrows from 'Visual Primitives' feed the later blocks. On the left, numbered training crops point to a cloud of numbered anchors. On the right, scattered patches connect to a primitive cloud of green dots. The eye goes first to the red-boxed failures.
caption: Few-Shot Atypical L2I via Semantic-Primitive Disentanglement. (a) Existing methods suffer from representation fragmentation, yielding geometric distortions and fragmented textures (\eg, deformed chimneys and turtles). In contrast, our method maintains structural coherence. (b) To address the granularity mismatch between semantic identity and visual details, we explicitly disentangle representations into Semantic Anchors and Visual Primitives, further guided by \CS to enforce foreground consistency.\fillpar
abstract: The layout-to-image (L2I) task enables fine-grained control over image generation via object categories and spatial layouts. However, existing L2I methods yield fragmented and distorted generations under few-shot atypical settings. We term this failure as representation fragmentation, arising from a granularity mismatch that entangles semantic identity with visual details. To address this issue, we propose a representation-driven framework that disentangles semantics from primitives for robust few-shot adaptation. Specifically, Semantic Anchoring aggregates categorical semantics into anchors for stable identity, while Primitive Imbuing models recomposable primitives for robust local detail modeling. Conceptual Steering further regulates optimization with a saliency-aware objective to preserve foreground semantic consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in the 5-shot regime over state-of-the-art L2I methods in both visual fidelity and alignment across diverse atypical domains. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/iCVTEAM/DSP.
